source.title: Gravity Optimizer: a Kinematic Approach on Optimization in Deep Learning

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is supplied
record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out performance across optimizers on natural image datasets, but uses different optimizers and does not compare adaptive methods with SGD or momentum SGD as V4 specifies.
record.gate_note: Reports optimizer comparisons on five datasets and two VGG architectures. Results are described in text and shown in figures; no numerical validation-accuracy values are supplied in the text. Hyperparameter descriptions and cited prior-work results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares Gravity with Adam and RMSProp, without an SGD or momentum-SGD baseline. These comparisons do not test V4's adaptive-versus-SGD claim or any other listed version. Citing original sources does not supply a test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The conclusion describes Gravity's experimental results as acceptable and proposes further evaluation. The abstract additionally claims greater stability and higher validation accuracy on CIFAR-100 Fine; these claims do not establish superiority across all tested settings.
record.recipe_differences: Compares a new optimizer, Gravity, with Adam and RMSProp using VGG16 and VGG19 on five natural image datasets; no random-label, width, architecture-family, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and VGG depth change the reported optimizer rankings and behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Across five image-classification tasks and two VGG depths, the authors report dataset-dependent validation rankings among Gravity, Adam and RMSProp. Gravity has higher validation accuracy on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 Fine, while Adam exceeds Gravity on MNIST/VGG16 and CIFAR-100 Coarse/VGG16. These are comparisons involving the study's proposed optimizer, without SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gravity can outperform Adam and RMSProp in held-out image-classification accuracy under the tested 100-epoch recipes, with rankings depending on dataset and architecture.

record.problems: The text gives qualitative descriptions of validation results but no numerical values or uncertainty estimates; figures are not accompanied by extracted values. Only two VGG depths and one batch size are evaluated. The paper states that no overfitting-prevention techniques were used.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: the optimizer comparisons do not test the specific SGD comparison required by V4. Figure-only values are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-versus-random-label held-out performance.
Generalization under widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional-versus-fully-connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance under limited tuning, and the stated effects of broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and language-model settings.
Batch-size effects and recipe changes that reduce large-batch penalties.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification and V4 tested_not_extracted status: no listed version is tested. Keeping rows empty is appropriate because the omitted optimizer comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out and do not match a claim version. VGG16 versus VGG19 changes depth, rather than testing V2's width claim.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
The reported comparisons are among Gravity, Adam and RMSProp, not adaptive methods versus SGD or momentum SGD; no language benchmarks, broader tuning, Adam-to-SGD switch, or decoupled weight decay.
No batch-size comparison or batch-size penalty is tested.
No dropout intervention or comparison is tested.
No sharpness or other generalization measure is evaluated.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
